info.title: FluxOS API v2
info.description:
The versioned FluxOS HTTP surface. v1 stays frozen and byte-identical for as long as it serves clients; v2 is additive and each endpoint is ported one at a time. Every v2 route lands with its entry here, and this file is the contract rather than a description of one.

NO CUSTOM VERBS. A state you can be IN is a state; a thing that HAPPENS is an operation. So run state is PUT to /apps/{name}/state, and everything else is created as an operation by POSTing to /apps/{name}/operations, read at /operations/{id} and cancelled by DELETEing it. PUT and POST already carry the difference: pressing stop twice is one state, pressing redeploy twice is two operations.

Path style is the subset express 4 and express 5 both accept: required path parameters only, no optional groups, no bare wildcards. An express 5 optional group registers on express 4 without throwing and then matches nothing, so the rule is enforced by tests/unit/routesV2.test.js.

tags.name: operations
tags.description: The status resource every long-running v2 operation points at.

tags.name: node
tags.description: This node's own process: how it came up.

get.description:
A running operation answers 200 with a non-terminal state. Completion is read from the body, never inferred from the status code: a failed operation is still a successful poll.

Unknown, expired and not-yours are deliberately one answer, so a caller cannot learn from the status code that someone else has an operation running.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The operation id, as returned in a 202.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Progress cursor. Only entries after this sequence number are returned.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

Retry-After.description: Present while the operation is still running.

post.summary: Deliver a paid app message this node is missing
post.description: Takes the contents of an app message whose payment this node's chain scan has recorded and for which it holds no message. Needs no authentication: contents that do not hash to a recorded payment, or fail a storage check, are not stored. A stored message is announced to the node's peers. The body is capped at 3 MiB.

200.description: This node already holds the message.

404.description: This node has recorded no payment for the hash.

422.description: The contents fail a storage check, or the body exceeds 3 MiB.

503.description: The node's local database or chain state is not ready.

get.summary: What this node holds about an app message
get.description: By the message's hash. `applied` and `refused` (with its `reason`) are this node's decision on the paid message; an applied answer names the `owner` and the `identity` the message gave the app. `unpayable` means this node held the message, its chain scan recorded no payment stamped within the hour after its signing, and the block that closed that window is deeper than any reorganisation the daemon accepts, so the chain can no longer pay it. `undecided` means this node holds the message, or a payment for it, and has decided nothing yet. 404 means this node holds nothing about the hash, which says nothing about the message: ask other nodes. Needs no authentication.

200.description: What this node holds about the message.

owner.description: Present when applied: the owner the message names.

identity.description: Present when applied: the identity of the app the message belongs to.

404.description: This node holds nothing about the hash.

503.description: The node's local database or chain state is not ready.

get.description: Every capability's state now and every transition the process has made since it started, each with when it happened, why, how long the state before it lasted (`tookMs`) and which prerequisite it was waiting on. `startedAt` is the process start, so a transition's `at - tookMs` is where its bar begins on a timeline from there. The last 2,000 transitions are kept. For the node's operator and the Flux team: the `zelidauth` header.

parameters.name: zelidauth
parameters.description: The node operator's or a Flux team member's signed login.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

now.description: When this answer was made, epoch milliseconds.

transitions.description: Every transition since the process started, oldest first.

tookMs.description: How long the state left behind lasted.

get.summary: What this node can do now
get.description: Every present capability's state, since when, why, how long the state before it lasted, what it waits on, and when it first came up in this process. For the node's operator and the Flux team: the `zelidauth` header.

parameters.name: zelidauth
parameters.description: The node operator's or a Flux team member's signed login.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

get.summary: Which capabilities held this boot up
get.description: Every present capability by how long after the process start it first came up, slowest first, with every capability that never has ahead of them all. What a capability waited on is the declared prerequisite that came up last before it did; one that never came up names what it waits on now. For the node's operator and the Flux team: the `zelidauth` header.

parameters.name: zelidauth
parameters.description: The node operator's or a Flux team member's signed login.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

upAfterMs.description: From the process start to its first rise; null while it never has.

comingUpMs.description: The part of it spent coming up, held below a prerequisite; null while it never has come up.

waitedOn.description: The declared prerequisite that came up last before it did, or what it waits on now while it never has come up.

get.summary: What decided when the boot finished
get.description: The chain of prerequisites that decided when the last capability to come up did: from the first link, which waited on nothing, to that capability. Each link is the declared prerequisite that came up last before the next one. For the node's operator and the Flux team: the `zelidauth` header.

parameters.name: zelidauth
parameters.description: The node operator's or a Flux team member's signed login.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

upAfterMs.description: From the process start to its first rise.

comingUpMs.description: How long it was coming up, held below a prerequisite, just before.

get.description: The capability transitions of this process and the processes before it, from a local collection that keeps the last 5,000 rows: newest process first, up to the last 10, each process's transitions oldest first. This process's transitions not yet written are included. For the node's operator and the Flux team: the `zelidauth` header.

parameters.name: zelidauth
parameters.description: The node operator's or a Flux team member's signed login.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

tookMs.description: How long the state left behind lasted.

503.description: The node's local database is not ready.

get.summary: The activeStandby components this node runs or holds
get.description: Each installed app's activeStandby component that this node is running, or holding (stopped by its operator, or being started by the reconciler), named by the app's identity and replica and never by component name. A component in neither state is absent. An app this node cannot read right now is listed by identity in `unreadable`, so absence from `components` means the component is not here.

parameters.name: X-Request-Id
parameters.description: Echoed back on the response and in meta.requestId. Minted when absent.

200.description: The components, and the apps this node cannot read.

replica.description: The named replica, null for a loose instance.

unreadable.description: Identities of installed apps this node cannot read right now.

503.description: The node's local database is not ready.

get.summary: Who has owned the app holding a name
get.description: The identity of the app that holds the name and each of its owners, in order, with the height at which they took it (the registration's height for the first). A past ownership is chain history and does not change, so a reader holding an owner's write, keyed by identity and the height its owner took the app, checks that owner against it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The app's name, in any letter case.

200.description: The app's identity and its ownerships.

identity.description: The identity of the app that holds the name.

from.description: The height at which this owner took the app.

404.description: No app holding the name has applied.

503.description: The node's local database or chain state is not ready.

post.summary: The fee consensus will charge a v9 app message
post.description: Prices a v9 registration or update as consensus will, fixed at the message's signed time: the rates in force an hour before that time, and for an update the unused share of the term it replaces at that time. A payment of `fee` satoshis mined by `payBy` is accepted whichever block confirms it. The body carries the fields the submission does; the client signs the message with the same `timestamp`. A private specification is sent sealed to this node's transport key exactly as it is submitted, with the `type` and `contentHash` its seal is bound to.

type.description: The message's type. Required with a sealed specification, whose seal is bound to it.

appSpecification.description: The message's specification, as submitted: in the clear, or sealed as { name, owner, transportEncrypted }.

contentHash.description: The message's content hash. Required with a sealed specification, whose seal is bound to it; when given, the specification priced must hash to it.

timestamp.description: The message's signed time, in ms; at most an hour old and five minutes ahead.

extend.description: The message's renewal flag: an update that sets it buys a new term and is never free.

usd.description: What a customer paying in dollars is charged; null with no oracle rate.

payBy.description: The latest block time, in ms, the payment can be mined at.

400.description: A field is missing or of the wrong type.

409.description: A message for this app is already waiting in this node's pool for its payment.

422.description: The timestamp is one a submission would refuse, the specification cannot be read, or the message is refused by name in `reason`: `NotQuotable` (a v1-v8 specification), `StampedEarly` (an update signed at or before the message it replaces), `UpdateRefused` (a free-shaped update with the free allowance spent), `PricingNotActive` (no price message is in force).

503.description: The node's pricing state, registry or chain state is not ready.

get.summary: The prices in force for a v9 app message
get.description: The rates and feature fees, the FLUX/USD rate and the price modifiers in force for a message signed at `timestamp`: exactly what a quote at that timestamp prices with. flux-spec-policy's `PricingEngine.from` builds the network's pricing engine from them.

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.description: The message's signed time, in ms; now when absent. At most an hour old and five minutes ahead.

pricedAt.description: The moment priced: the signed time in seconds and the next block's height.

prices.description: The price message's values in force: commodity rates in microdollars, feature fees, minimums and the standard period.

fluxUsdPriceE4.description: FLUX/USD × 10000; null with no oracle rate in force.

modifiers.description: The price-modifier values in force: duration buckets, instance tiers, fiatMarkupBp, updateDiscountBp.

400.description: The timestamp is not an integer.

422.description: The timestamp is one a submission would refuse, or no price message is in force (`reason`: `PricingNotActive`).

post.summary: Checks an app message before it is signed and paid for
post.description: Holds a registration or an update to the checks its submission will apply: the specification, the name, the update's invariants, and whether the network can place it. Takes the fields the submission carries, without its signature. A private specification is sent sealed to this node's transport key exactly as it is submitted, with the `type` and `contentHash` its seal is bound to.

type.description: The message's type; selects the checks a registration or an update is held to.

version.description: The message's envelope version: 1 for a v1-v8 specification, 2 for v9.

appSpecification.description: The message's specification, as submitted: in the clear, or sealed as { name, owner, transportEncrypted }.

contentHash.description: The message's content hash. Required with a sealed specification, whose seal is bound to it.

timestamp.description: The message's signed time, in ms.

appSpecification.description: The specification as the node will broadcast it.

400.description: `type` or `appSpecification` is missing or of the wrong type.

422.description: The message is refused; `message` gives the reason its submission would.

503.description: The node's registry, chain state or explorer is not ready.

post.summary: Stores and broadcasts a signed app message
post.description: Stores a signed registration or update and broadcasts it to the network, answering its hash once this node holds it. The message is applied once its payment confirms; its decision is read at the `Location` answered.

type.description: The message's type; selects the checks a registration or an update is held to.

version.description: The message's envelope version: 1 for a v1-v8 specification, 2 for v9.

appSpecification.description: The message's specification, as submitted: in the clear, or sealed as { name, owner, transportEncrypted }.

contentHash.description: The message's content hash. Required with a sealed specification, whose seal is bound to it.

timestamp.description: The message's signed time, in ms.

signature.description: The owner's signature over the message.

hash.description: The message's hash, the reference its payment carries.

400.description: `type` is missing or not a message type.

401.description: The caller is not a signed-in user.

422.description: The message is refused; `message` gives the reason.

503.description: The node's registry, chain state or explorer is not ready, it holds too few peer connections to broadcast the message, or it broadcast the message and does not hold it yet. The message can be submitted again.

zelidauth.name: zelidauth
zelidauth.description: The signed FluxID auth header. Semantics are identical to v1; v2 only moves the check from the handler into middleware.

requestId.description: On every answer, success or error, and echoed in the X-Request-Id header.

status.description: Running, Succeeded, Failed or Canceled. Terminal status is read from here, not from the HTTP code.

progress.description: Append-only. Use the since cursor to read only what is new.

Error.description: Mutually exclusive with data: an answer carries one or the other, never both.

code.description: The stable machine-readable contract. The HTTP status is derived from it, so the two cannot disagree.

Accepted.description: The 202 every long-running v2 action answers with. Location carries the same statusUrl.

owner.description: The service that raises and lowers it.

needs.description: The capabilities it is held below until they are up.

waits.description: The capabilities the code bringing it up waited for.

since.description: When it entered this state, epoch milliseconds.

lastTookMs.description: How long the state before this one lasted; null before its first transition.

waitingOn.description: The first prerequisite not up, or itself while its owner has not raised it; null when up.

firstUp.description: Its first rise in this process; null while it never has.

comingUpMs.description: How long it was coming up, held below a prerequisite, just before; 0 when it rose straight from down.

Error.description: An error, in the one envelope.
